chunks: Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Sa'dan, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I heard him saying: 'Fever is the harbinger of death, and it is the prison of Allah in the earth, and it is the believer's share from the Fire.'

key_terms.الحمّى: Fever — understood here not merely as a physical ailment but as a spiritually significant trial
key_terms.حظّ المؤمن من النار: The believer's share from the Fire — fever substitutes for the believer's portion of hellfire punishment
key_terms.رائد الموت: Harbinger/herald of death — the fever announces and prepares one for death
key_terms.سجن الله في الأرض: Prison of Allah in the earth — fever confines and restricts the person as a divine decree

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the spiritual significance of fever in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) teaches that fever serves a profound spiritual purpose: it is a foretaste and herald of death, a form of divine confinement in this world, and — for the believer — a means of expiation from the punishment of the Hereafter. This hadith reflects the Shia theological tradition that worldly suffering, particularly illness, can serve as atonement (kaffarah), substituting for the believer's portion of the hellfire they might otherwise face in the next world.
